exploration.title: Solar System Explorer
exploration.subject: Space science
exploration.summary: Compare the eight planets at equal elapsed time and on one diameter scale.
exploration.question: What changes when planets are compared for the same elapsed time or on the same diameter scale?
exploration.explanation: The Sun’s gravity keeps eight planets in orbit. A year is one planet’s complete orbit, so planets with different orbital periods complete different fractions in the same elapsed time. One astronomical unit (AU) is about Earth’s mean distance from the Sun. Planet diameters and Sun–planet gaps differ so greatly that a useful screen model must show them on separate scales.

experiments.title: Hold elapsed time fixed
experiments.instruction: Predict whether Earth, Neptune or both complete the same orbit fraction in one Earth year. Select your prediction, then compare one Earth year.
experiments.observe: Earth completes 1.000 orbit and Neptune about 0.006 orbit (1/165). Explain why equal elapsed time does not mean equal orbital fractions.

experiments.title: Hold diameter scale fixed
experiments.instruction: Predict whether Jupiter is about 5, 11 or 50 Earth diameters across. Select your prediction, then compare Earth and Jupiter.
experiments.observe: Jupiter’s equatorial diameter is about 11.21 Earth diameters. Explain why a separately framed close-up cannot establish this ratio.

exploration.misconception: A convenient orbit picture does not show true planet sizes and true gaps on one common scale. The model’s circular paths and starting positions are illustrative, not today’s sky.
